headline: Chip Rout Sours Friday's Close as Gulf Tensions Frame the Week Ahead
body_html:
Wall Street ended the week on a weak note in Friday's session, October 30. Of the 530 stocks we track, 344 fell and only 182 rose. Semiconductors took the brunt of the selling, dropping 6.04%, and materials (down 1.75%), industrials (down 1.56%) and healthcare (down 1.29%) also lost ground.

A few corners held up. Homebuilders gained 1.75% and energy added 0.44%. Individual moves were large in both directions. Capri Holdings jumped 16.31% and Cavco Industries rose 13.11%, while Roblox sank 18.05%, Bright Horizons fell 17.92% and Twilio lost 15.24%. Software slid 1.14% as a group.

Traders head into Monday, November 2, with geopolitics high on the agenda. Iran's navy says four tankers caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, and Iranian envoys have met Qatari mediators amid talk of possible US strikes after the midterms. Germany's record-low gas storage adds to the energy picture. Whether Friday's chip selling spreads or fades is the first test of the week.

briefs.headline: Chip sector suffers its worst session in the universe
briefs.body: Semiconductors fell 6.04% on Friday, far more than any other group we track. Memory name Sandisk dropped 13.47% and optical-networking supplier Coherent lost 11.34%. Monday will show whether buyers step in or the selling carries over into the new week.

briefs.headline: Software and online names take heavy hits
briefs.body: Twilio fell 15.24% and Datadog lost 11.5%, helping drag the software group down 1.14%. Roblox, in internet gaming, was the single biggest decliner at 18.05%. The stock-specific damage was far deeper than the sector averages suggest.

briefs.headline: Housing-linked stocks buck the downturn
briefs.body: Homebuilders led all sectors with a 1.75% gain. Cavco Industries surged 13.11% and flooring maker Mohawk Industries climbed 7.25%. Housing-related shares were a rare area of strength in a session where most stocks fell.

briefs.headline: Sharp rebounds for Capri, GoDaddy and others
briefs.body: Capri Holdings led all gainers with a 16.31% jump, followed by GoDaddy at 10.72%. Donnelley Financial rose 9.53% and CoStar Group gained 7.21%. The winners came from varied industries, pointing to company-specific news rather than a single theme.

briefs.headline: Hormuz fire reports and Iran talks keep energy in focus
briefs.body: Iran's IRGC Navy says four tankers caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz. Separately, Iranian envoys met Qatari mediators as a threat of US strikes looms after the midterms. Energy stocks rose 0.44% on Friday, and traders will watch for further developments.

briefs.headline: Germany's gas cushion looks thin heading into winter
briefs.body: A lobby group says Germany needs to do more to rebuild gas reserves, with storage at a record low. The warning comes as Gulf tensions already weigh on energy sentiment. European supply security is likely to remain a theme in the days ahead.
